# Repository cooking notes (for AI coding assistants)

This file contains concise, actionable guidance for AI agents working in this repository. Focus on the files and commands referenced below when making edits, running, or debugging.

- Project type: multi-module Gradle Java application (JavaFX UI in `app/`).
- Gradle wrapper: use the root `gradlew`/`gradlew.bat` (Windows PowerShell: `./gradlew` -> `.\gradlew.bat`).

Key locations
- `app/`: main application module (JavaFX UI). Main class: `com.team.translator.App` (see `app/build.gradle`).
- `app/src/main/java/`: primary Java source tree. Example: `com/team/translator/Translator.java`.
- `app/src/main/resources/`: runtime resources used by the app.
- `app/scripts/` and `app/bin/`: packaging and runnable scripts generated by the Gradle `application` plugin.
- `app/javafx-lib/`: populated by `:app:copyJavafxLibs` to help local debugging with JavaFX module path.

Important integrations and runtime assumptions
- The app calls a local translation backend at `http://127.0.0.1:5000/translate` (see `Translator.java`).
  - HTTP POST JSON body shape: `{ "q": "text", "source": "en", "target": "es", "format":"text" }`.
  - The code expects a JSON response with a `translatedText` field. If the backend is not running the
    app will get connection errors.
  - Before running or testing translation flows, ensure the translation service (likely LibreTranslate
    or a local Flask app) is running on port 5000.

Build / run / test (Windows PowerShell examples)
- Build the whole project: `.\gradlew.bat build`
- Run the `app` module: `.\gradlew.bat :app:run` (runs `com.team.translator.App` via the `application` plugin)
- Run tests (module): `.\gradlew.bat :app:test` or all tests: `.\gradlew.bat test`
- Prepare JavaFX jars for VS Code debugging: `.\gradlew.bat :app:copyJavafxLibs` (this creates `app/javafx-lib`).

Conventions & patterns to follow
- Java toolchain: project uses Java 21 via Gradle toolchains (see `app/build.gradle`). Keep source/target compatibility consistent.
- Native libraries and platform specifics: project depends on OpenCV (`org.bytedeco:opencv-platform`) and Tess4J
  (`tess4j`) — these can bring native dependencies. Test native-path and platform behavior on Windows.
- JSON handling: `com.google.gson.Gson` is used across the codebase. When parsing HTTP responses the code expects
  standard JSON objects (see `Translator.java`). Preserve current JSON field names in API calls unless adapting both sides.
- UI: JavaFX controls are used. For debugging, prefer launching with the `copyJavafxLibs` task and adding
  `--module-path` to the Java launch config so JavaFX modules are resolvable.

What to check before editing code that integrates with external services
- Confirm the external service contract matches the code (field names, status codes). Example: `Translator.translate`
  expects `translatedText` in the response JSON. If the backend changed, update the Java parsing accordingly.
- If adding retries or async behavior to network calls, prefer small, well-tested changes and keep network I/O off the
  JavaFX UI thread.

Files to inspect for context when making changes
- `app/build.gradle` — build plugins, JavaFX plugin config, main class, and `copyJavafxLibs` helper.
- `app/src/main/java/com/team/translator/Translator.java` — HTTP translation client; shows expected payload and response.
- `app/src/main/java/com/team/translator/App.java` — app entrypoint (start here for UI flow).
- `app/scripts/` and `app/build/distributions/` — packaging artifacts and start scripts generated by Gradle.

Editing rules for AI
- Keep changes limited and localized: prefer editing only files needed to implement a feature or fix.
- Preserve project Java version (toolchains) and build scripts unless the user explicitly requests a version bump.
- When touching native/third-party libs (OpenCV, Tess4J), add testing notes and platform-specific guards.

If uncertain, ask the developer for:
- Whether the translation backend is LibreTranslate or a custom service, and whether its API changed.
- Preferred way to run the app locally (Gradle run vs. a packaged distribution).
